heading: Long-term care insurance, traditional or hybrid (72 seconds)
name: Long-term care insurance: traditional or hybrid?
description: Traditional long-term care insurance is pure care coverage, while a hybrid pairs care benefits with life insurance or an annuity. This short video compares premiums, what happens if care is not needed, and questions to ask.
transcript: Long-term care insurance: traditional or hybrid? Here is how the two types differ. Long-term care is help with daily living, such as bathing, dressing or eating. It can happen at home, in assisted living or in a nursing facility. A traditional policy is pure long-term care coverage. It pays toward covered care if you meet the policy's benefit triggers. A hybrid combines care benefits with life insurance or an annuity. Traditional: premiums can rise. Generally nothing returned if care is not needed. Generally more care coverage per premium dollar. Hybrid: premiums are often guaranteed. A death benefit if care is not needed. And a higher upfront cost. How important is premium certainty? Is maximum care coverage the priority? Does leaving something to heirs matter? Benefits and eligibility depend on the policy. Traditional premiums are not guaranteed. Guarantees depend on the insurer's claims-paying ability.
